nodes.name: Execute Workflow Trigger
nodes.notes:
Called by all upstream components (WF-04, WF-06, RA-01 through RA-06).
Expected input: { case_id: BIGINT, signal_name: string }
Valid signal_name values: documents_ready | kyc_ready | references_ready |
  ra01_ready | ra02_ready | ra03_ready | ra04_ready | ra05_ready | ra06_ready |
  meetings_ready | afp_ready

parameters.query:
UPDATE car_case_gate_inputs
   SET {{ $json.signal_name }} = TRUE
 WHERE case_id = '{{ $json.case_id }}'
RETURNING case_id, {{ $json.signal_name }} AS updated_flag;

nodes.name: Postgres: Set Signal Flag
nodes.notes:
Dynamic column name injected from signal_name. n8n executes this via
parametrised query pre-processing. The UPDATE returns the row so we can
verify the write succeeded before proceeding.

parameters.query:
SELECT
    case_id,
    documents_ready,
    kyc_ready,
    references_ready,
    ra01_ready,
    ra02_ready,
    ra03_ready,
    ra04_ready,
    ra05_ready,
    ra06_ready,
    meetings_ready,
    afp_ready,
    required_inputs,
    gate_triggered_at
FROM car_case_gate_inputs
WHERE case_id = '{{ $('Execute Workflow Trigger').item.json.case_id }}'

nodes.name: Postgres: Read All Flags
nodes.notes:
Read the full current state after the update so the Code node
has an accurate snapshot to evaluate.

nodes.name: Code: Evaluate Gate Condition
nodes.notes:
Pure evaluation — no DB writes. Checks all required flags and whether
the gate has already been triggered (idempotency guard).

nodes.name: IF: Gate Condition Met?
nodes.notes:
TRUE branch: all required flags are set AND gate has not yet fired.
FALSE branch: either condition fails — silently exit (no error).

parameters.query:
-- SELECT FOR UPDATE serialises concurrent transactions.
-- If two signals arrive simultaneously, one waits here while the other
-- completes the UPDATE and COMMIT. The waiting transaction then re-reads
-- gate_triggered_at and finds it non-NULL, so it skips the UPDATE.
BEGIN;

SELECT gate_triggered_at
FROM car_case_gate_inputs
WHERE case_id = '{{ $json.case_id }}'
FOR UPDATE;

UPDATE car_case_gate_inputs
   SET gate_triggered_at = NOW()
 WHERE case_id = '{{ $json.case_id }}'
   AND gate_triggered_at IS NULL
RETURNING case_id, gate_triggered_at, required_inputs;

COMMIT;

nodes.name: Postgres: Lock & Set gate_triggered_at
nodes.notes:
Atomic lock + write. Uses SELECT FOR UPDATE so only one concurrent
transaction can fire the gate. The WHERE gate_triggered_at IS NULL
clause means a race-winning second writer produces 0 rows returned,
which the next IF node catches.

nodes.name: IF: Lock Won (Row Returned)?
nodes.notes:
If the UPDATE returned a row, this transaction won the race and should
fire the main gate flow. If 0 rows returned, another transaction already
set gate_triggered_at — silently exit.

nodes.name: Execute: WF-07-C Main Gate Flow
nodes.notes:
Fire-and-forget (waitForSubWorkflow: false) so this sub-workflow returns
immediately to the caller. The main gate flow runs asynchronously.
Replace WF-07-C-DD-GATE-MAIN with the actual n8n workflow ID after import.

nodes.name: Code: No-Op (Gate Not Met)
nodes.notes:
Silent exit. Logs the case_id for debugging. Returns empty array
so n8n shows 0 items and no error.

nodes.name: Code: No-Op (Race Lost)
nodes.notes:
Handles the case where SELECT FOR UPDATE was obtained but the conditional
UPDATE affected 0 rows (gate_triggered_at was already set by a concurrent
transaction that committed first).
